title: Completion factor from an explicit finite subalgebra agreeing away from an element
statement: Let R be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], S any commutative R-algebra and q a prime of S. Suppose an R-subalgebra S' of S is a finite R-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], g ∈ S' is outside q, and the canonical away-localization map S'_g → S_g is bijective [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Put p = q ∩ R, Rp = R_p and Sq = S_q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let Rph and Sqh be their maximal-ideal-adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let f : Rp → Sq be the induced local homomorphism and ι : S → Sqh the composite of the canonical localization and completion maps. Write Ip and Iq for the maximal ideals of Rp and Sq. For any ring map ψ : Rph → Sqh such that, for every n ≥ 0, x ∈ Rph and a ∈ Rp, the nth coordinate of x being the class of a modulo Ip^n implies that the nth coordinate of ψ(x) is the class of f(a) modulo Iq^n, put U = Rph ⊗_R S. There exist a commutative ring B in the universe of U, ring maps β : U → B and φ : U → Sqh, and a ring equivalence e : U ≃ Sqh × B, such that φ(x ⊗ y) = ψ(x)ι(y) on pure tensors and e = (φ, β). The finite subalgebra and its away-isomorphism are inputs, not conclusions; this omits their construction from quasi-finiteness.

proof.text: For each r in R, use the given levelwise formula on the completion image of r and the localization base-map identity. Completion extensionality shows psi commutes with R. Regard psi and the natural S to Sqh map as R-algebra maps and use the tensor universal property to construct phi, with the prescribed formula on every pure tensor.

Apply finite_completion_factor_idempotent to this phi. It supplies e,v in T, e^2=e, v gamma=e, phi(j(e))=1, surjectivity of phi j, and its zero-kernel implication e t=0. These are data on the finite tensor only.

Away-map surjectivity gives z,n with z=g^n y for every y in S. Tensor induction gives for each u in U a t in T and n with j(t)=j(gamma)^n u. The zero tensor has exponent 0. A pure tensor x tensor y uses x tensor z. For a sum with numerators tx,ty and exponents n,m, use gamma^m tx + gamma^n ty and exponent n+m.

Set delta=j(e). For every n, delta j(v)^n j(gamma)^n=delta by v gamma=e and idempotence. If phi(x)=phi(y), clear denominators of x-y as j(t)=j(gamma)^n(x-y). Then phi(j(t))=0, so e t=0. Applying j and multiplying by j(v)^n gives delta(x-y)=0. Conversely delta x=delta y implies phi(x)=phi(y) because phi(delta)=1.

Construct B as the corner ring of the complementary idempotent 1-delta, and beta(u)=(1-delta)u. The pair (phi,beta) is injective by the preceding equivalence and u=delta u+(1-delta)u. Given (c,b), choose t with phi(j(t))=c. The element delta j(t)+b maps to (c,b), since phi vanishes on the complementary corner. RingEquiv.ofBijective of the pair gives the required equivalence and its ring-hom equality is reflexive.

theorem completion_split_of_finite_subalgebra_away
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (q : PrimeSpectrum S)
    (S' : Subalgebra R S) [Module.Finite R S']
    (g : S') (hg : g.1 ∉ q.asIdeal)
    (haway : Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap S'.val.toRingHom g)) :
    let p : Ideal R := q.comap (algebraMap R S)
    let Rp := Localization.AtPrime p
    let Sq := Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal
    let Ip := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal Rp
    let Iq := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal Sq
    let Rph := AdicCompletion Ip Rp
    let Sqh := AdicCompletion Iq Sq
    let f : Rp →+* Sq := Localization.localRingHom p q.asIdeal (algebraMap R S) rfl
    let U := TensorProduct R Rph S
    ∀ (ψ : Rph →+* Sqh),
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Rph) (a : Rp),
        AdicCompletion.evalₐ Ip n x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ip ^ n) a →
        AdicCompletion.evalₐ Iq n (ψ x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Iq ^ n) (f a)) →
      ∃ (B : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing B) (β : U →+* B) (φ : U →+* Sqh),
        (∀ (x : Rph) (y : S),
          φ (TensorProduct.tmul R x y) =
            ψ x * algebraMap Sq Sqh (algebraMap S Sq y)) ∧
        ∃ e : U ≃+* Sqh × B, e.toRingHom = RingHom.prod φ β
